Please solve this issue: Finance writes off invoices that will never be paid. Add `write_off(invoice, at, reason)` to `ledgerly/adjustments.py`: it marks an issued invoice as `"void"` and returns a dict with the keys `invoice_id`, `amount` (the invoice total) and `reason`. Only issued invoices can be written off.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0002] Normalize unit prices with to_money: Wrap raw line unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before multiplying by quantity, and seed sums with the ZERO constant from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input in ledgerly/invoice.py by raising BillingError(code, detail) with the established codes: "invalid_state" for wrong invoice status, "invalid_quantity" for bad quantity, "negative_amount" for negative prices.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Exclude bool when validating integer fields: When validating integer inputs like quantity in ledgerly/invoice.py, check isinstance(x, bool) first because bool is a subclass of int and True would otherwise pass as 1.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize any incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

## Code review of your previous attempt
Your previous attempt at this issue was reviewed and not accepted. The repository still contains that attempt. Address every comment below:
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
